messages:
Sam (AM): Quick note 1 BetaHealth POC is blocked on observability handoff. Logs are flowing but nothing is linking to their traces; also seeing intermittent Splunk 403s and occasional 429s.
Rina (SE): Can you paste a raw log line and a sample trace id from their APM so I can compare?
Sam (AM): Sample log: 
  2026-03-15T09:45:12Z lvl=info msg="resp complete" route=/api/chat trace=abcd1234efgh user=beta-42
Trace id present as "trace" in body; their spans show a different trace id format and don't join.
Rina (SE): Likely header mismatch or header stripping. Our collector uses x-request-id / traceparent / b3. Do they expect something custom (e.g., X-BH-TRACE)? @Luca any whitelist rules on the proxy?
Luca (SRE): By default the edge strips unknown headers for safety. We only forward: x-request-id, traceparent, b3, and authorization. Custom headers require per-tenant enablement.
Rina (SE): Two ways: 1) enable a tenant mapping to copy the structured trace into X-BH-TRACE on outbound so their APM will join; or 2) they add a log pipeline rule to extract trace= and inject into spans. Which is easier for Beta?
Sam (AM): They cannot change the app but can change the edge router. They requested we inject X-BH-TRACE header outbound.
logs-bot: Drain job 4712 -> FAILED (403) to https://ingest.beta.splunk:8088 (attempt 2)
reason: invalid-token or header-rewrite
Sam (AM): They tested the token in Splunk UI and it works. Could be their proxy rewriting Authorization to something else. I asked them to run a curl from their edge.
Maya (Eng): Our drain client sends header: Authorization: Splunk <token>. Also note we apply a default rate_limit_per_tenant: 15/s and exponential backoff. If the upstream rewrites Authorization to drop creds it will 403.
Rina (SE): Sharing our drain config (internal): 
```
collector:
  drain:
    type: http
    url: https://ingest.beta.splunk:8088/services/collector/event/1.0
    headers:
      Authorization: "Splunk <REDACTED>"
      X-Customer-ID: "beta-42"
    max_retries: 4
    retry_policy: exponential
    rate_limit: 15/s
    buffer_ms: 2000
```
Ask them to try both Authorization and X-Splunk-Token variants.
Sam (AM): They ran curl and got 403 when we proxy, but 200 from a laptop. They suspect their edge rewrites Authorization.
Maya (Eng): If their edge rewrites Authorization, advise them to accept X-Splunk-Token or allow Authorization passthrough. We can also send the token in X-Splunk-Token header as a workaround.
Sam (AM): Also they asked about retention for the POC 10d is too short, they want 60d for a month. Any temporary option?
Maya (Eng): We can grant a one-week 60d retention window for POC at no extra charge; billing will be noted if extended.
Luca (SRE): I'll enable the per-tenant header whitelist for beta-42 and add a mapping to inject X-BH-TRACE copied from "trace" field. I'll also bump their rate_limit to 60/s for 24h for validation. Plan to roll in ~12 minutes and monitor.
logs-bot: Drain job 4713 -> SUCCESS to datadog-forwarder (latency 142ms)
Sam (AM): Security question from Beta: can we use their KMS for encrypting logs in a Private deployment? They want exact wording for the security questionnaire.
Maya (Eng): For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and can integrate with their key provider. For Hosted, we offer BYOK options for sensitive fields via our KMS integrations. I'll paste SOC2/KMS wording into the questionnaire and send.
Sam (AM): Next steps:
- Luca to flip header-whitelist + inject X-BH-TRACE and bump rate (in progress)
- Maya to update sec questionnaire and enable temporary retention window
- Rina to send curl examples (Authorization + X-Splunk-Token) to Beta and #sales
- Sam to run validation call 2026-03-15 13:00 UTC with BetaHealth
Rina (SE): I'll drop the curl examples after the deploy. Quick curl for them to run: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Splunk <their-token>" -H "X-Request-ID: 999" https://ingest.beta.splunk:8088/services/collector/event/1.0
```
Sam (AM): Thanks all 1 I'll update Beta and keep this thread live. :thumbsup:
